45_marg2985: The word of God, which always comes down to the prophets, comes also to Micheas, whose name means “humility”; to Micheas of Morasthi, which to this day is a small village near Eleutheropolis, a city of Palestine, and whose name means “heir.” And beautifully humility, which is foremost among the virtues, is born of the hope of God's inheritance. Here is not meant the humility that comes from the consciousness of sins, but that which is counted among the virtues. Hence it is said: “Be you humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God”; and: “he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted”; and the Lord: “learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.” So as among us names are given as a wish and as it were an omen of virtue, for example Victor, Castus, Pius, Probus, and common nouns are turned into proper names, so among the Hebrews too Micheas and Abdias and Zacharias and the like were given to children by their parents from the names of virtues.

45_marg3011: Make thee bald. Allegorically. These things can be taken of the overthrow of the Jews by the Romans: O Judea, who once flourished before God but have now cried “Crucify, crucify,” put off the hair of your glory, for you have no prophets, nor the protection of angels, nor teachers of the law. It can also be referred to the whole human race: O human soul, who once enjoyed delights in paradise and had beautiful hair, and are now cast down into the Babylonian captivity, shave yourself and take the garb of a penitent; and you who flew on high like an eagle, mourn your sons who are taken captive. For this the Lord devises a most grievous evil against you. And because your glory has been shaved off, O soul fallen from paradise through Adam, or from the Church through your own sin, saints are sent to weep for you who sin and do not repent; for they see others possessed by fornication, avarice or murder, and fields once holy handed over to the Assyrians and the king of Babylon, over which God does not stretch his cord.

45_marg3075: Let the mountains hear. The mountains are the “ministering spirits,” to whom the care of human affairs has been entrusted. He is bidden to contend in judgement against these, so that, if those mountains or hills are found not to have cared well for the people, it may be seen whether the fault is God's, who set unfit ones over them; or the angels' own, if they did not do what belonged to their office; or the people's, who scorned to obey good overseers. And since no fault can be found either in God or in the angels, it remains that it is found in the people, and that they are justly punished. Yet God does not want to bring punishment on sinners at once by his power; but, so as to be seen to be just, he calls the sinners to judgement, so that, with the angels and all creation as witnesses, they may answer if they can allege anything against God.

Those who at some time serve Pharaoh and the Egyptians in clay and brick, if their redeemer at some time argues with them, let them not neglect the voice of him who rebukes, but know that God sends before them Moses, that is, the spiritual law; and Aaron, that is, Christ the high priest; and Mary, that is, the prophecy of the prophets. And he also delivers them from the hand of Balach, whose name means “licking out,” that is, the devil, who longs to destroy, who is king of those who abuse the law. Balaam means “a vain people,” Beor “drive out.” When the devil, through the vain people of the Gentiles, sprung from “drive out,” that is, given up to the works of the flesh, wants to curse man, God on the contrary compels him to bless. 45_marg3087: Allegorically. Hear, you who are signified by the ten tribes, which divided themselves from the kingdom of David and the worship of the temple. And who will approve your separating yourselves from the Church of God? There is still in you the fire of anger and lust, you who are the house of the wicked devil; and in you are the devil's treasures, that is, because you fraudulently gather the riches of the Scriptures; and in you the measure of judgement is less than it ought to be, and therefore full of the wrath of God. For I will not justify the balance, that is, those who pervert judgements for a person or for money, which is understood by the weights of the bag; by which the rich are filled, that is, when for the sake of filthy gain they judge not according to the case but according to the difference in wealth. And moreover the inhabitants of that city, which they build up with depraved teachings, are liars. Therefore, O city which the heretics build, I will strike you so that you perish from your wickedness; you who eat by reading the Scriptures and are not filled, because you are empty of truth; and your humiliation is in the midst of you, because in your conscience you feel that you are failing for want of spiritual food. You will indeed take hold of many depraved teachings, but, understanding the error, you will see that you cannot be saved in them; and whoever of your citizens think they can be saved in them, I will give to the sword, that is, I will instruct them by punishments. So, O city most wicked in iniquity and with a deceitful balance, built by heretics, you will sow by sinning and not reap by profiting in your hearers; you will tread the olive and not anoint your head with the flattery of sinners; nor will you make drunk those who drink the wine of Sodom. And this because you have kept the commandments of Amri, and every work, namely of the demons or of those who were heresiarchs, and have walked in their wills, that is, in a depraved teaching invented not by God's will but by theirs. And therefore you will perish from your heresy, and your inhabitants will be gathered to me as I hiss for them; and then you will bear, that is, you will recognise that you have borne, the reproaches and sins of many peoples.
